transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-12
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 47 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Markus (Arcadia Head of ML), Sonia (Arcadia Platform Eng), Tom (Arcadia CTO)

Summary:
Quick walk-through of Redwood model catalog and compatibility matrix, talk through benchmarking plan, clarify Arcadia's constraints (VPC, data residency, latency SLO), and agree next steps for a short pilot. SE demo focused on console filters, bench spreadsheet, and how runtime choices (Dedicated, Hosted, Private) affect cost/latency.

Topics covered:
- Catalog filters and compatibility matrix
- Bench plan + required artifacts
- Networking / VPC / private deployment constraints
- Security / compliance questions (SOC2 / SSO / KMS)
- Pricing and pilot options (Dedicated vs hosted)

[00:00] Evan: all right good afternoon everyone thanks for joining uh this is Evan from Redwood, i'm joined by Priya our solutions engineer. quick round of intros?
[00:12] Markus: hey i'm Markus, Head of ML at Arcadia, so we're the analytics platform that powers our customer's dashboards and a lot of generative summarization flows.
[00:18] Sonia: Sonia, platform eng, i'll be owning the infra side—networking, security, etc.
[00:22] Tom: Tom here, CTO, i'll be in the background but want to validate the architecture fit.
[00:28] Evan: great. agenda for today is a targeted demo of the catalog + compat matrix, show how we pick open models, share bench plan. we'll leave time for security questions and next steps. sound ok?

[02:05] Priya: all right i'm going to share the console. so this is the Redwood Console — you'll see the model catalog on the left, we've got filters for architecture, quantization, hardware compatibility, and typical benchmarks. for Arcadia i'd highlight the "latency-sensitive" preset which tunes for short inference 1-step responses.

[04:20] Markus: quick question, when you say hardware compatibility is that per-GPU family or per-kernel? we run mixed T4 and A10 fleets in gcp today.
[04:33] Priya: short answer is both — the compat matrix maps model variants to kernel sets and recommended hardware. for example, a quantized 4-bit variant might be fine on A10s but on T4 you'd hit different perf profiles. the console shows the recommended mapping and an estimated token p100 per second. uh — p100 is a poor transcription there — it's tokens per second estimate.

[06:20] Evan: also note we surface expected latency percentiles for 128-token prompts and cost per 1k tokens on that mapping. that helps you make the latency vs cost tradeoff.

[08:12] Sonia: can you show an example model pick? we were looking at a shortlist: Mistral family, a couple of LLaMA reworks, and a 7b distilled option.
[08:27] Priya: sure — here's the shortlist view. you can pin different models and run a side-by-side bench. i'll open the bench tab — you'll see we capture throughput, p50/p95 latency, memory footprints and quality proxies. note the quality proxies are small evals we ship with the catalog — they are not a replacement for your prod evals.

[12:10] Priya: also, for Arcadia's use case where you do short summarizations in real time we usually recommend enabling prefix caching — we call it KV cache prefetch in some places but the transcript may say K-V cash — it's the same thing. it dramatically reduces token re-compute for repeated contexts.

[14:30] Markus: on caching — we have multi-tenant streams with user-specific contexts, is there risk of cross-tenant leakage with prefix caches?
[14:45] Priya: good callout. our KV cache is tenant-scoped and pinned per model instance; in dedicated/private deployments you get stronger tenant isolation and you control the cache lifecycle. we can show logs that validate cache partitioning during the POC.

[18:00] Tom: security wise we need SOC2, SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS integration for keying. can you confirm what you provide for Private?
[18:16] Evan: yes for Redwood Private we support customer-managed KMS (Cloud KMS or HSM), SAML SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and full audit logs. our SOC2 report is in the security pack, i'll send that over.

[20:05] Sonia: network-wise we need VPC peering or private link and strict egress controls; we are not allowed to touch PII outside our VPC.
[20:19] Priya: Private supports VPC peering and an on-prem package for air-gapped setups. for hosted we have private endpoints as well. we'll note the exact requirements and recommend either Private with your infra or a VPC peering test for the pilot.

[24:30] Priya: switching back to bench plan — we usually ask for a 1–2k prompt sample, an expected traffic profile (p50 calls/sec), and quality targets. then we run a three-phase bench: baseline, shortlist runs, and a focused p95 latency study. i'll drop the bench spreadsheet after this call — it has suggested prompts, config columns (batching, max tokens, quantization), and run instructions.

[26:10] Markus: for metrics we care about p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, and a small quality rubric—ROUGE for summarization but we also want a few human sample checks.

[30:05] Priya: that aligns. one thing to flag — batching has a big impact on cost but can hurt latency. Redwood Optimize (sometimes mis-transcribed here as Redwood Opti-mize) suggests batching policies and quantization combos per workload. for real-time summarization we'd likely keep batch small and use a lower latency kernel.

[32:48] Sonia: what's the quickest path to run an on-site latency check — we prefer a dedicated pool for predictable SLAs.
[33:02] Evan: Dedicated pools give you reserved GPU capacity and predictable throughput; you can start with a small monthly commit for a pilot. we can also do an on-demand short bench on hosted to validate before committing. Dedicated also gives better isolation and faster cold-starts for KV cache.

[36:40] Markus: curious about fallback routing — if my preferred model has no capacity, can requests fall back to a higher-latency cheaper variant? we need graceful degradation.
[36:52] Priya: yes, smart routing supports variant fallback. you define policy priority — like prefer low latency model, fallback to a quantized variant, then to a cheaper model. all of that is visible in route configs and traces in the Console.

[40:00] Tom: pricing — we need a ballpark for the pilot: 50k tokens/day with p95 target under 400ms.
[40:12] Evan: i'll run numbers but rough — if you run a small dedicated pilot and pick an optimized 7b quantized model, costs will be lower than using large hosted LLMs. i'll send a few scenarios: hosted baseline, dedicated pilot, private on-prem option.

[42:15] Sonia: on compliance docs — can you attach SOC2, pen-test summary, and a sample contract redline?
[42:26] Evan: yep i'll include those — SOC2 + SSO/KMS integration docs and our standard enterprise terms.

[44:00] Markus: would like to see a sample bench run results — do you have an example spreadsheet?
[44:09] Priya: yes, i'll share a sanitized bench example from a previous summarization workload. you'll get the raw csv and a pivot with p95/p50 stacks plus config columns.

[46:00] Evan: ok summarizing next steps — Priya will share bench spreadsheet and a sanitized example, i'll follow up with pricing and security pack, Arcadia will confirm VPC/peering contact and dataset access, and we'll set up a 2-hour scoping session next week. any other asks?
[46:22] Tom: no that's it, thanks.
[46:26] Markus: thanks everyone.
[46:30] Evan: great talk soon — we'll follow up via email with action items. bye.

References mentioned:
